Overview of the organization: The Chief Operating Office (COO) Technology organization is responsible for defining and executing technology strategy, roadmap, and GenAI adoption across Core Operations, Corporate Shared Services, Controls, and enterprise GenAI initiatives. The COO Technology capability sits within CIO organization reporting into the CIO and COO of the firm.  The organization ensures strategic alignment of solutions across a diverse portfolio of cross business and functional capabilities such as KYC, Fraud, Cash Management, Reconciliations, and Regulatory Reporting. It also drives the modernization of enterprise applications and process reengineering through shared services, comprehensive data architecture, automation, and adoption of Generative AI solutions. Corporate Shared Services is a newly established capability within COO organization, reporting directly to the COO of the firm. It is responsible for all non-client-facing operations , including - Cash Services (Payroll & Supplier Strategy, Cash Management, Bank Network Management, Payment Controls & Processing Risk and Client Asset Oversight), as well as Balance sheet substantiation and Reconciliation, Non-Financial Regulatory Reporting and International Operations. Job Purpose: The Head of Corporate Shared Services Technology will be a key leader in the COO technology organization and across the broader CIO organization. They will be responsible for designing, developing and execution for the overall architecture vision and strategy for cross-business operations functions including – cash management, payments control services, global reconciliations, non-finance reg. reporting, and payroll. We are seeking a visionary leader to standardize, simplify, and scale a current fragmented application landscape to deliver business value and drive efficiencies. This role requires deep experience in designing, executing, and managing complex systems on a scale, a passion for architectural simplification, and a demonstrable commitment for building sustainable, future-ready platforms. Driving enterprise adoption of GenAI solutions including large language models and agentic flows is a critical component for executing the vision.  The successful candidate will partner with SMEs across business, Operations, Finance, and Technology functions and transformation leads to develop architecture blueprints, end-to-end systems design, operating model, and multi-year GenAI execution roadmap. The role reports directly into the Head of Technology COO. Role Summary The Head of Corporate Shared Services Technology is a senior leadership role accountable for owning and driving the technology book of work supporting all the functions under Corporate Shared Services. This individual will serve as the primary technology counterpart to the Head of Corporate Shared Services, providing dedicated, executive-level engagement to ensure the seamless integration of technology strategy with business priorities. This leader will act as a strategic technology advisor across architecture and risk, bringing an enterprise mindset to simplify, modernize, and strengthen the Controls technology landscape. The role is responsible for translating COO business strategy into a clear, executable multi-year technology roadmap and ensuring disciplined delivery with measurable business outcomes. The position combines portfolio leadership, delivery execution, and senior stakeholder engagement, with accountability for governance, funding, value realization, and regulatory alignment across a complex, high-impact portfolio. Responsibilities Portfolio Strategy & Planning Own and maintain the multi-year technology roadmap aligned to Corporate Shared Services strategic priorities, enterprise architecture, finance targets, and risk mandates. Lead annual planning and quarterly reprioritization cycles, including intake, scoping, sizing, dependency mapping, sequencing, and funding alignment. Translate business outcomes into prioritized technology initiatives with clear ROI and measurable impact. Ensure a strong linkage between strategy, execution, and value realization. End-to-End Delivery Leadership Lead cross-functional delivery spanning engineering, product, architecture, cyber, risk & compliance, data, and operations. Drive execution discipline across the SDLC and adjacent governance processes (requirements, design reviews, testing, release, and change management). Ensure production readiness, operational stability, and high-quality delivery outcomes. Proactively manage dependencies, critical paths, and risks to ensure on-time and on-budget execution. COO Technology Partnership & Governance Serve as the primary technology point of contact and dedicated executive-level partner for the Head of Corporate Shared Services and Head of COO Technology. Develop and deliver executive-level communications, including steering committee materials and portfolio updates to improve decision-making speed and reduce execution risk. Lead governance forums including Steering Committees, Portfolio Review Boards, and Architecture Review Boards. Ensure transparency, accountability, and alignment across all stakeholders. Drive the adoption of shared services across the enterprise in partner with other CIO leads. Architecture, Risk & Controls Advisory Act as a strategic advisor on architecture and risk, bringing an enterprise-wide perspective to Corporate Shared Services technology. Drive simplification and consolidation of the Corporate Shared Services technology ecosystem. Partner closely with Controls, Risk, and Compliance stakeholders to ensure robust, scalable, and compliant solutions. Embed strong risk and control frameworks into all phases of technology delivery. Innovation, Automation & Efficiency Identify and deliver AI-driven and automation opportunities across Corporate Shared Services, including generative AI, predictive analytics, workflow intelligence, and RPA. Lead efficiency and productivity programs targeting improvements in cycle time, quality, throughput, and cost-to-serve. Organizational & Financial Leadership Lead and develop a high-performing global organization (including teams of circa 100+ professionals) through multiple layers of management. Establish optimal team structures, roles, and operating models aligned to business and technology priorities. Drive a culture of accountability, inclusion, innovation, and continuous learning. Manage the technology portfolio budget (circa $100mm), ensuring effective funding allocation and cost discipline, and drive financial transparency across all initiatives. Optimize vendor strategy, including strategic sourcing, partnerships, and outsourcing. Qualifications 15+ years of relevant experience in technology, with a proven track record of leading large-scale application development organizations. 10+ years of managerial experience, including managing senior leaders and large, global teams. Proven track record in delivering enterprise utilities, shared services in financial services. Hands on expertise in financial services and operations preferred. Experience with liquidity, cash management, reconciliations, reporting strongly preferred. Significant experience in a senior technology leadership role, acting as a strategic partner to senior business executives. Demonstrated ability to build and maintain strong peer and business relationships. Advanced knowledge of industry practices, standards, rules, and regulations within the financial services sector. Expertise in software development processes and practices (SDLC), with a strong focus on execution discipline. Demonstrated knowledge of architecture, complex systems, and key technology areas within funds administration. Proven track record and mature understanding of adoption of GenAI solutions beyond PoCs, and pilots. Strong working knowledge of risk, controls, and compliance frameworks. Strong communication skills and ability to decompose complex requirements into simple concepts to bring people along the journey on a shared vision. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.  Job Overview  Job Purpose: To provide legal support to Markets businesses in connection with Rates and Markets Treasury businesses. Job Background/context: The role is dedicated to the Rates and Markets Treasury businesses globally with focus in the North America and LATAM country clusters. It covers all desks within the Rates and Markets Treasury businesses, with primary interaction being with: (i) the NAM Corporate Solutions Group; (ii) the Rates and Markets Treasury structuring team; (iii) the Local Markets Rates business in NAM & LATAM; and (iv) the businesses providing bespoke/structured funding and/or hedging solutions to clients. This is a role requiring a broad range of legal skills, ranging from an understanding of secured and deal-contingent hedging to the ability to understand and structure complex, bespoke trades in different legal forms (e.g. securities lending, derivatives, loans, deposits). It will also require a working knowledge of ISDA definitional booklets, such as the Rates and Credit Definitions, knowledge of relevant regulations such as Dodd Frank, US Risk Retention, securities laws and Volcker, and experience with issues raised by transactions in emerging / local markets. Familiarity with applicable capital rules will also be helpful. The successful candidate must therefore have the ability to work with, and perform the role of a senior adviser to, multiple desks with varying technical requirements across the derivative and SFT spectrum. They must also be able to work collaboratively with senior stakeholders in Risk, Finance, Compliance and other areas, as well as seniors within Legal, on the strategic aspects of supporting the relevant businesses. This role is currently expected to have four or five direct reports within the RMT Legal team, some located in New York and some in Europe. Thus the role will include being both an escalation point for technical questions on relevant topics as well as performing formal management duties for the team. Accordingly, the successful candidate will also be expected to be willing and able to take an active role in the career and technical development of junior colleagues, working with the Global Head to develop the wider team as a whole where relevant. However, should any candidates wish to be considered for a role without management responsibilities this can be discussed as part of the recruitment process. Key Responsibilities The candidate will be expected to cover a wide range of transactions and advice as a senior adviser across various desks, including: Bespoke financing structures, including repo financing, derivatives-based financing (particularly TRS), collateralisation structures, financial guarantees and margin loans Technical elements of derivative documentation, including close-out provisions, optional and mandatory termination provisions, cash settlement calculations, and bespoke payoffs Syndicated swap arrangements, e.g. risk participation agreements Secured hedging, including being able to explain to stakeholders (in the business as well as other stakeholders such as Risk and ICM) the nuances of certain points and also to work with more junior colleagues on relevant points Contingent hedging, including those relating to M&A, issuance, and project finance Repackaging transactions across a variety of underlying product classes, including knowledge of relevant rules and exemptions, such as securities rules (144A, 4(a)(2), Reg S), investment company act exemptions (3a-7, 3(c)(1), 3(c)(7)), commodity pool exemptions and implications for US Risk Retention Non-linear derivatives, particularly swaptions and inflation-based products Advising on the 2006 and 2021 ISDA Definitions and the 2003 and 2014 ISDA Credit Definitions (as applicable) General advice on disputes and queries arising from OTC transactions Stable value Regulatory aspects relating to the above, including applicable sections of Dodd Frank, Volcker, and other relevant regulations Training and supporting colleagues on the above Working on escalations with the Global Head of Rates & Markets Treasury Legal and, as relevant, the Global Head of Markets Legal Development Value: This is an excellent opportunity for a senior lawyer with a broad range of technical skills who enjoys dealing with a broad and changing diet of complex, technical work. Knowledge of both derivatives and SFTs is important, but this role could suit a candidate with an emphasis or background in either one of these areas. The successful candidate will be a subject-matter expert and senior adviser across a number of products and desks, and will function as a key point of senior escalation on day-to-day matters for the wider team. They will work directly with the Global Head on other points of escalation and broader strategic goals for the relevant businesses. This role as designed will also benefit someone looking to demonstrate and develop their managerial skills, and provides the opportunity to do that on a global scale. Person Specification Knowledge/Experience: Preference for a candidate with: At least 8 years’ post-qualification experience, ideally with experience of working in-house. Experience of structuring complex transactions is preferred, including the underlying treatment of such trades (e.g. regulatory characterization, capital, credit, XVA). Skills/Competencies Candidate must have: Ability to work independently and efficiently. Ability to work under pressure. Excellent organisation skills. Ability to present complex issues simply to senior management (legal and business). Ability to interact with and train junior colleagues Fluent in English (written and oral). Interest in technology. title: Head of Program Management - Wealth
description_text: Head of Program Management - Wealth   Apply (opens in new window)  Save       Job Req Id:  26980028    Location(s):  New York, New York, United States    Job Type:  Hybrid    Posted:  Jul. 21, 2026       Discover your future at Citi  Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.  Job Overview  Citi Wealth is seeking an exceptional Head of Program Management to join our Content & Client Engagement team — and to build the operational backbone of something genuinely ambitious. This is a senior leadership role that sits at the intersection of creative production and institutional rigour. Think of it as a Supervising Producer at the highest level of the craft — with the fiscal authority, operational scope, and strategic influence of a COO. You will be the force that turns creative ambition into delivered reality: on time, on budget, on standard, across every format the team produces. The Content & Client Engagement team is a growing, entrepreneurial undertaking inside one of the most powerful financial institutions in the world. The creative output is broad and genuinely varied — social content, short-form and long-form video, podcasts, whitepapers, research brochures, executive presentations, live events, client experiences, installations, and more. The standards are high. The environment is regulated. The pace is real. And the person who holds this role will be the reason it all runs. You will report directly to the Head of Content & Client Engagement and work in close, day-to-day partnership with the Director of Strategy — functioning as the operational counterpart to strategic vision. Where the Director of Strategy identifies the stories emerging from across the Wealth Management organisation, you are the person who translates them into tangible outputs at the speed of markets. That high-rate metabolism is a defining characteristic of the role. You are built for it. At the same time, you bring equal command to the team's calendar of established obligations — marquee conferences and events, quarterly investment reports, annual surveys and flagship research publications — planning and resourcing them with the same precision you bring to the fast-moving, real-time output that runs alongside them. You hold both tempos simultaneously, without dropping either. You are also the person who closes the loop. Every piece of content this team produces is an investment — in the brand, in client relationships, in the business pipeline — and you treat it as one. You build and continuously refine the measurement frameworks that track the impact of that investment, folding the learnings back into how the team plans, resources, and makes decisions. You are always looking for better tools, better signals, and better questions to ask of the data. You have spent your career producing complex, multi-format media at scale. You have priced campaigns that span disciplines, assembled the teams to execute them, delivered in high style, and overseen the measurement of their impact. You are as comfortable negotiating a vendor contract as you are building an annual budget from first principles or navigating the permitting requirements for a drone shoot in three jurisdictions. You bring a deep rolodex, consummate vendor relationships, and an instinct for when to build in-house and when to bring in the best of the outside world. Critically, you balance your on-time, on-budget fixations with a genuine commitment to quality and differentiation. You are not here to make things cheaper. You are here to make things possible — and to make them excellent. This is a C14 SVP-level role reporting directly to the Head of Content & Client Engagement, with authority across the full production pipeline, resource allocation, vendor relationships, budget ownership, and performance measurement for the team. Responsibilities: Production Operations & Pipeline Management Own and manage the end-to-end production workflow for the Content & Client Engagement team — across all formats, all markets, and all stages of production simultaneously. Design and maintain a production pipeline that gives the team clarity on what is in development, what is in production, what is in post, and what is live — at any given moment. Implement and operate the best available campaign and production management tools to provide real-time visibility across multiple concurrent productions — and deliver regular, structured cadence reporting to leadership on status, risks, resource utilisation, and delivery timelines. Manage two distinct production tempos in parallel: the high-rate, market-responsive output that emerges from the team's ongoing strategic intelligence, and the established calendar of marquee events, quarterly reports, annual surveys, and flagship publications — ensuring both are planned, resourced, and delivered with equal rigour. Anticipate production bottlenecks, resource conflicts, and scheduling risks before they become problems — and resolve them when they do. Build and maintain production processes, workflows, and standards that scale as the team grows — without adding bureaucracy that slows the creative work down. Strategic Partnership with the Director of Strategy Work in close, daily partnership with the Director of Strategy — functioning as the operational engine that converts strategic editorial priorities into production reality. Translate stories, themes, and content opportunities identified from across the Wealth Management organisation into costed, resourced, scheduled productions — moving from brief to output at the speed the market demands. Maintain a shared view of the content pipeline with the Director of Strategy — ensuring that editorial ambition is always calibrated against production capacity, resourcing, and budget in real time. Contribute to strategic planning and content calendar development — bringing a producer's eye to what is feasible, what requires investment, and what needs to flex. Measurement, Impact & Continuous Improvement Own the team's measurement framework — establishing how the impact of every project is tracked, evaluated, and reported, from content engagement and audience reach through to contribution to the business pipeline and client relationship development. Treat measurement as a discipline, not an afterthought — building it into production planning from the outset, so that every project launches with clear success metrics and exits with a clear performance record. Conduct rigorous post-project retrospectives and synthesise performance data into actionable learnings — feeding those learnings directly back into how the team plans future productions, allocates resources, and makes investment decisions. Continuously improve the accuracy, depth, and relevance of the team's measurement capability — staying ahead of available tools and methodologies, and adopting new platforms and approaches as they emerge. Build and maintain regular performance reporting for senior stakeholders — translating content metrics into business-relevant language that connects creative output to commercial outcomes. Resource Planning & Allocation Lead all resource planning for the team — allocating internal talent, managing capacity, and identifying gaps that require external support. Match the right people — internal and external — to the right projects, balancing creative fit with operational efficiency. Build and maintain a deep, reliable network of external production specialists, freelancers, and agencies across disciplines — cinematography, editing, design, motion graphics, audio, events, experiential, and beyond — available to deploy at short notice and at the right level of quality. Advise on staffing and team structure as the function grows — with a clear view of where investment in permanent headcount is warranted versus where a flexible external model makes more sense. Budget Ownership & Fiscal Management Author, own, and manage the team's overall annual production budget — with the rigour, transparency, and accountability that a regulated financial institution demands. Build detailed project-level budgets for individual productions and campaigns — from first estimate through to final reconciliation — across the full format spectrum: video, audio, print, digital, events, experiential, whitepapers, executive presentations, and more. Develop clear, substantiated investment cases for new initiatives, capability builds, and significant production expenditures — presenting them with the financial literacy and institutional credibility required to secure approval at senior levels. Track spend in real time, identify variances early, and manage the team's resources with genuine fiscal discipline — without sacrificing quality as a default cost-saving measure. Ensure all production expenditure complies with Citi's procurement, contracting, and vendor management policies. Vendor & Third-Party Management Own all vendor relationships on behalf of the Content & Client Engagement team — from boutique production houses to major event suppliers to specialist post-production facilities, print and publishing vendors, and research distribution partners. Negotiate, structure, and manage contracts with third-party suppliers — ensuring the team gets best value, appropriate protections, and consistently high performance from its external partners. Conduct regular vendor performance reviews and maintain a tiered supplier ecosystem that the team can draw on with confidence. Identify, evaluate, and onboard new specialist suppliers as the team's production ambitions evolve. Compliance, Permissions & Regulatory Diligence Operate with precision in Citi Wealth's high-profile, highly regulated environment — ensuring that every production is legally compliant, properly permitted, and fully risk-assessed before it goes into production. Own all permitting, licensing, releases, and regulatory requirements across production types — including location and event permitting, talent and music licensing, image and data rights, drone operation regulations across multiple jurisdictions, data privacy considerations for filmed content, broadcast and distribution rights, and print and digital publishing compliance. Partner with Citi's legal, compliance, and risk teams proactively — building relationships and processes that protect the team without creating unnecessary friction in the creative workflow. Maintain current knowledge of relevant regulations across the team's key markets — New York, London, Hong Kong — and ensure production practices are consistently aligned. Team Leadership & Senior Collaboration Operate as a senior leadership presence within the Content & Client Engagement team — contributing to strategic planning, team culture, and the overall direction of the function alongside the Head of Content & Client Engagement. Build strong working relationships with internal stakeholders across Citi Wealth — including investment, marketing, legal, compliance, technology, and communications — to ensure productions are well-supported, well-informed, and institutionally aligned. Mentor and develop junior production and project management talent within the team. Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency, as well as effectively supervise the activity of others and create accountability with those who fail to maintain these standards. Qualifications: 10+ years of professional experience in production management, project management, or operations leadership within a multi-format media, content, advertising, events, or broadcast environment — with a portfolio that spans the full range: social content, short-form and long-form video, podcasting, whitepapers, research publications, executive presentations, brochures, live events, installations, and 360-degree campaigns. A proven track record as a 360-degree campaign veteran — someone who has priced it, assembled the team, executed in high style, and overseen the measurement of impact across genuinely diverse production formats and disciplines. Demonstrated experience managing two-speed production environments — high-rate, market-responsive output running in parallel with a structured calendar of flagship events, quarterly publications, and annual research programmes. A proven and rigorous approach to content measurement — with experience building or significantly evolving measurement frameworks that track impact from content engagement through to business pipeline contribution, and a track record of using those learnings to sharpen future production decisions. Exceptional fiscal literacy — with direct experience authoring and owning significant production budgets, building investment cases, and managing spend with institutional-grade rigour and transparency. Deep expertise in production operations — pipeline design, resource planning, scheduling, vendor management, and real-time production tracking using professional campaign and project management platforms. Consummate vendor and third-party management skills — including contract negotiation, supplier performance management, and the ability to build and maintain a high-quality, reliable external production ecosystem. Comprehensive knowledge of production compliance and regulatory requirements — including location and event permitting, talent and music licensing, image and data rights, drone regulations across multiple jurisdictions, and broadcast and digital distribution licensing. A deep and current network of production specialists, freelancers, agencies, and suppliers across disciplines — deployable at the right quality level, at short notice. Outstanding organisational skills and an exceptional eye for detail — in a regulated financial environment, the details are not optional. Strong communication and stakeholder management skills — equally effective presenting a budget to a CFO, briefing a production crew, or partnering with a senior strategist on content priorities. A genuine commitment to quality and creative differentiation as production values — not just as aspirations. Education: Bachelor’s/University degree, Master’s degree preferred This job description provides a high-level review of the types of work performed. Other job-related duties may be assigned as required. Preferred Qualifications Experience producing content within financial services — ideally wealth management, private banking, or asset management — with an understanding of the regulatory, reputational, and brand considerations that environment demands. Proven experience working in close operational partnership with a strategy or editorial leadership function — translating strategic priorities into production realities at pace. Experience operating within or alongside a regulated institutional environment — with established relationships with legal, compliance, and risk functions. Familiarity with AI-assisted production management tools, content performance analytics platforms, workflow automation, and real-time campaign reporting systems — and a proactive approach to adopting new measurement tools as they become available. Experience building or scaling a production function from an early stage — defining processes, establishing supplier ecosystems, and growing a team. International production experience — managing productions across multiple markets, time zones, and regulatory jurisdictions simultaneously. MBA or equivalent advanced degree — or demonstrable equivalent through career achievement. Core Competencies Operational Mastery: You run complex, multi-format production operations with the precision of a seasoned COO. Nothing falls through the cracks because you designed the system that catches it. Two-Speed Fluency: You manage high-rate, market-responsive production and a structured calendar of flagship obligations simultaneously — holding both tempos without losing discipline or quality in either. Strategic Partnership: You are the operational counterpart to creative and editorial vision. You work hand in glove with strategy leadership to make ideas real — quickly, resourcefully, and at the right standard. Measurement Discipline: You close the loop on every project — tracking impact, synthesising learnings, and feeding them back into how the team works. You treat measurement as a craft, stay current with available tools, and are always looking for a more accurate, more useful signal. Fiscal Authority: You own budgets with the confidence and rigour of a finance professional — building investment cases, tracking spend, and making the numbers work without sacrificing the work. 360-Degree Production Range: Your career spans the full spectrum — social, short and long-form video, podcasting, whitepapers, research publications, executive presentations, live events, experiential, and beyond. You have priced it, built it, delivered it, and measured it. Vendor Excellence: Your external relationships are among your most valuable professional assets. You manage them with respect, hold them to a high standard, and know exactly who to call. Regulatory Precision: You operate in complex, regulated environments without flinching — understanding that compliance is not a constraint on ambition but a condition of it. Quality Under Pressure: You are fixated on on-time and on-budget delivery — and equally fixated on ensuring those fixations never become a reason to produce work that is merely adequate. Senior Leadership Presence: You carry the authority, credibility, and composure of a C-suite operator. You lead by example, develop the people around you, and earn trust across the organisation. ------------------------------------------------------ Job Family Group: Marketing ------------------------------------------------------ Job Family: Digital & Social Media Marketing ------------------------------------------------------ Time Type: Full time ------------------------------------------------------ Primary Location: New York New York United States ------------------------------------------------------ Primary Location Full Time Salary Range: $163,600.00 - $245,400.00 In addition to salary, Citi’s offerings may also include, for eligible employees, discretionary and formulaic incentive and retention awards. Citi, the leading global financial services company, has some 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. Citi provides consumers, corporations, governments and institutions with a broad range of financial products and services, including consumer banking and credit, corporate and investment banking, securities brokerage, and wealth management. Citi Bank Retail Mortgage provides home lending services via our Citibank branches and centralized service centers. This highly interactive role engages internally with retail branch partners, operations, community business development officers. This role drives mortgage sales and client relationships through engagement with clients, real estate agents, and other area referrers. Responsibilities: Consult with customers about their financial situation, financial and personal objectives and lending needs for the purpose of helping them achieve their home ownership goals. Make recommendations to customers about which lending solutions would best meet the customers' financial and personal objectives Advise customers about the consequences, risks, and benefits of alternative lending solutions. Visit customers outside of Citi's offices, with such visits to vary based on clientele, geography, market conditions, and other factors. Work as a team with all internal partners to support and grow our customers. Refer customers who seek financial services other than lending solutions to the appropriate Citi professionals. Partner with Operations teams to ensure the seamless transfer of the loan application in order to provide documents to the Processors and acquire any additional information needed by the Processors and/or Underwriters. Recognized technical authority for an area within the business. Requires basic commercial awareness. There are typically multiple people within the business that provide the same level of subject matter expertise. Significant impact on the area through complex deliverables. Provides advice and counsel related to the technology or operations of the business. Work impacts an entire area, which eventually affects the overall performance and effectiveness of the sub-function/job family. Responsibilities: Framework Implementation and Oversight: Lead the implementation and ongoing enhancement of the country risk management framework, ensuring alignment with global enterprise policies (LTMP, ECRM policy) and the firm's risk appetite statement. Independent Review and Challenge: Act as a key 2nd LOD partner to the Franchise CCOs, RMCOs and IBCRM. Provide independent, forward-looking assessments and credible challenge on strategic initiatives, new products, and significant transactions to ensure country-specific risks are fully identified and mitigated. Stress Testing and Scenario Analysis: Contribute significantly to the country risk stress testing and scenario planning processes for Country specific bespoke rapid stress tests. Analyze the potential impact of severe but plausible scenarios on your portfolio and use the results to inform contingency planning and risk mitigation strategies. Policy and Process Enhancement: Serve as a subject matter expert, contributing to the periodic review and enhancement of the Cross-Border Risk Policy, Cross- Border Calculation Procedure and associated Product Programs, and other key governance documents to ensure they remain relevant and effective. Limit Management: Proactively analyze the risk profiles of assigned countries to develop and present comprehensive recommendations for changes to country limits (including cross-border, notional, and stress loss) to senior risk management. This is an ideal role for someone looking to leverage their technical background to build a solid expertise in risk-management; alternatively someone with a strong risk background seeking direct exposure and ability to impact the commercial side of the business. description_text: Director, Services Operations AI Governance & AI-First Ways of Working   Apply (opens in new window)  Save       Job Req Id:  26986994    Location(s):  New York, New York, United States, Tampa, Florida, United States    Job Type:  Hybrid    Posted:  Aug. 14, 2026       Discover your future at Citi  Working at Citi is far more than just a job. A career with us means joining a team of approximately 219,000 dedicated people from around the globe. At Citi, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, give back to your community and make a real impact.  Job Overview  At Citi, you won't be running a typical IT implementation. You'll be at the center of redefining how one of the world's largest financial institutions actually operates — from the inside out. Services Operations touches millions of client interactions, thousands of associates, and some of the most complex workflows. You'll have the mandate, the access, and the executive backing to deploy AI where it matters most: at the point where our people serve our clients. The problems are real, the scale is unmatched, and the impact is immediate and measurable. Citi is looking for a Director, Operations AI Governance & AI-First Ways of Working to lead the governance, prioritisation, and adoption of AI across Citi's global Operations function. This is a senior leadership role with end-to-end accountability for managing the Operations AI use case pipeline — ensuring that investment is aligned to strategic priorities, that AI capabilities are adopted consistently, and that the function builds the organisational behaviours needed to operate in an AI-first way. This role is for a senior operations leader who understands that the hardest part of AI transformation is not the technology — it is the governance, the culture, and the discipline to ensure that the right things get built, adopted, and sustained. If you combine strategic thinking with practical delivery experience and a passion for embedding technology-driven change across large, complex organisations, this role offers the mandate and platform to make a lasting impact. Responsibilities Own the Operations AI intake process from end to end — evaluating, prioritising, and governing AI use cases to ensure investment decisions are grounded in strategic objectives and measurable business value. Drive AI-first ways of working across Operations, accelerating capability adoption, embedding new tooling into day-to-day practice, and leading the organisational change needed to shift how teams operate. Chair cross-functional Operations forums, bringing together leaders from Product, Technology, Risk, Compliance, and Operations to reach well-informed prioritisation and governance decisions. Partner with Product leads to align use case prioritisation across functions, ensuring Operations requirements are reflected in platform and capability planning. Define and track adoption metrics, engagement indicators, and business outcomes across AI capabilities, using data-driven insights to continuously improve utilisation and value realisation. Support the transition of Operations towards AI-first product development practices, guiding teams through tooling adoption and embedment as ways of working evolve. Lead multiple senior operations managers across large or distributed teams, setting clear performance expectations and making decisions on hiring, development, and organisational structure. Required Qualifications & Skills 15 or more years of experience in operations or a related function, including at least 8 to 10 years leading large, matrixed teams through other managers. Demonstrated ability to govern complex, cross-functional programmes — with full accountability for outcomes, planning, budgets, and strategic direction across multiple teams. Clear track record of leading organisational change and capability adoption at scale, translating strategic priorities into operational practice across large teams. Strong commercial awareness and analytical capability, including the ability to evaluate AI use cases against risk, reward, and business value criteria to inform investment decisions. Ability to assess and manage risk in business decisions, maintaining consistent standards for compliance, controls, and sound ethical judgement that protect the firm and its clients. Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with experience influencing senior stakeholders across functions and building alignment around shared priorities. Profile We are looking for candidates who fit one or more of the following profiles: Operations or Operations Technology Leaders: Professionals who have led technology-enabled transformation within operations functions at large regulated institutions — with a deep understanding of what it takes to govern AI adoption responsibly across high-volume, compliance-sensitive environments. AI/Automation Program Leaders: Senior leaders who have owned governance, prioritisation, and intake frameworks for AI and intelligent automation programmes within operations contexts — ensuring the right use cases get resourced and the right outcomes are tracked. Transformation Leaders: Individuals who have driven AI-first culture change across large operations organisations — embedding new ways of working, accelerating tooling adoption, and sustaining behavioural change beyond the initial launch phase. Key Attributes Operational Empathy: Has walked in the shoes of an operations team. Understands the day-to-day realities of SLAs, case management, escalation paths, and the human impact of getting automation wrong — and uses that empathy to make better governance decisions. Pragmatic Technologist: Possesses strong working knowledge of AI — including LLMs and agentic frameworks — but filters every technical decision through the lens of operational feasibility, auditability, and risk. Can credibly partner with both product/engineering teams and operations leaders. This role plays a critical part in enabling business growth, risk management, regulatory compliance, customer acquisition, and digital transformation initiatives through the delivery of scalable, secure, and innovative technology solutions. As demand and portfolio complexity continue to increase, this position serves as a key technology and business partner responsible for bridging strategic business objectives with technical execution. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor and liaison across Product, Business, Technology, Architecture, Operations, Data, Risk, and Vendor teams to ensure business needs are translated into well-defined solutions that drive measurable business value. This individual will leverage deep expertise in application development, systems analysis, business analysis, data integration, and technology delivery to guide initiatives from concept through implementation and post-production adoption. This role requires a unique combination of technical expertise, business acumen, analytical problem-solving, leadership, and stakeholder management skills to successfully navigate a highly complex environment with multiple priorities, dependencies, and regulatory considerations. Key Responsibilities Strategic Technology & Business Partnership Partner closely with business leaders, product owners, technology teams, architects, and operational stakeholders to align technology investments with strategic business priorities. Support the delivery of initiatives that improve customer acquisition, customer engagement, marketing effectiveness, credit risk management, and operational efficiency. Translate strategic business goals into actionable technology roadmaps, requirements, and implementation plans. Act as a trusted advisor to business and technology leadership by providing insights, recommendations, and solution alternatives that balance business value, risk, cost, and technical feasibility. Participate in portfolio planning, investment prioritization, capacity planning, roadmap development, and strategic technology discussions. Business Analysis & Requirements Leadership Lead the discovery, analysis, documentation, and validation of complex business, functional, technical, data, and non-functional requirements. Collaborate with architecture and engineering teams to design scalable, resilient, and future-ready solutions. Evaluate current-state systems and identify opportunities for modernization, automation, process optimization, and technical debt reduction. Define and validate system impacts, data requirements, integration points, dependencies, and solution architecture considerations. Provide guidance on application design decisions to ensure alignment with enterprise architecture standards, security requirements, and technology strategies. Review technical specifications and designs to ensure accurate implementation of business requirements. Ensure solutions comply with corporate policies, security standards, regulatory obligations, and control frameworks. Partner with Risk, Compliance, Audit, and Control teams to address findings, remediation activities, and control requirements. Maintain transparency through proactive communication, issue escalation, and risk management practices. Leadership, Collaboration & Influence Serve as a subject matter expert across business processes, systems, and technology capabilities supporting Acquisitions, Marketing, and Risk functions. Mentor and coach business analysts, technology analysts, and project team members to promote best practices and continuous improvement. Drive alignment among diverse stakeholder groups with competing priorities and objectives. Influence decision-making through data-driven analysis, business cases, and technology recommendations. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, and delivery excellence. Required Qualifications 6+ years of experience in Application Development, Systems Analysis, Technical Business Analysis, Product Delivery, or related technology disciplines. Proven experience delivering complex enterprise technology solutions from requirements definition through implementation. Strong technical foundation with the ability to understand application architectures, APIs, databases, integrations, cloud technologies, and software engineering concepts. Extensive experience gathering, documenting, validating, and managing business, technical, process, and data requirements. Experience leading cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, systems, and delivery teams. Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate complex business and technical issues. Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management capabilities. Experience with Agile, Scrum, SAFe, Waterfall, or hybrid delivery methodologies. Knowledge of customer acquisition funnels, digital marketing platforms, campaign management technologies, decision engines, and customer onboarding processes. Experience working with cloud platforms, microservices architecture, APIs, event-driven architecture, and modern application ecosystems. Understanding of data governance, data management, reporting, analytics, and AI-enabled business capabilities. Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Confluence, SQL, Visio, Azure DevOps, Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms. Experience supporting large-scale modernization, transformation, or regulatory programs within financial services. Success Factors The ideal candidate will demonstrate: Strategic thinking and business acumen. Technical depth and systems analysis expertise. Ability to lead through influence rather than authority. Strong ownership mentality and execution focus. Exceptional stakeholder partnership and communication skills. Ability to simplify highly complex business and technical concepts. Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on innovation and efficiency. Strong risk awareness and commitment to operational excellence. Passion for delivering technology solutions that drive measurable business outcomes and customer value. Job Overview  About the Role Join the Controls Technology division as a Technology Product Owner. In this critical role, you will act as the bridge between complex business needs and our engineering teams. You will be empowered to translate intricate requirements for risk and control systems into a flawlessly managed backlog of epics and user stories. Your primary mission is to drive the delivery of high-quality, compliant software by ensuring our development teams have the clarity and context needed to execute effectively, sprint after sprint. This is a role for a product owner — someone who thrives on execution, champions quality, and is passionate about building world-class technology solutions in a dynamic, global financial environment. What You'll Do 1. Backlog Ownership & Agile Execution Own and Master the Backlog: Meticulously create, refine, and prioritize the product backlog, ensuring it is transparent, well-understood, and always ready for at least two sprints ahead. Translate Vision into Action: Deconstruct complex business requirements into well-defined Epics, User Stories, and precise Acceptance Criteria, ensuring a high percentage of stories are accepted without rework. Drive Sprint Success: Serve as the dedicated point of contact for the engineering team, providing unwavering clarity during sprint planning, daily stand-ups, and throughout the development cycle to remove ambiguity. 2. Solution Definition & Quality Assurance Define the "What": Partner with business stakeholders to elicit, analyze, and document requirements, defining the precise solution to be built. Champion Quality: Drive a quality-first mindset with a relentless focus on clear, testable acceptance criteria to minimize ambiguity and reduce critical defects in UAT. Demonstrate Value: Conduct compelling demos of new functionalities to stakeholders, showcasing the value delivered and gathering immediate feedback for iterative improvement. Track Performance: Track and report product performance post-launch to evaluate outcomes and support decisions around future investment. 3. Stakeholder Collaboration & Domain Leadership Build Partnerships: Act as the key liaison between business users, engineering teams, UX and other technology partners, fostering a collaborative environment to ensure seamless delivery; seeking continuous input from stakeholders and incorporating it into the backlog. Become the SME: Develop a deep expertise in your assigned Controls Technology modules, becoming the recognized go-to subject matter expert for the team and key stakeholders. Facilitate with Purpose: Lead and actively contribute to all agile ceremonies, ensuring refinement and planning sessions are efficient, productive, and outcome focused. Dependency & Risk Management: Identify and manage cross-team and cross-platform dependencies early in the delivery lifecycle. Proactively highlight delivery risks, data dependencies, and integration challenges, and work with stakeholders to drive timely resolution. Communicate Clearly: Communicate priorities, dependencies, risks, and delivery status clearly to stakeholders and leadership. Support informed decision-making by articulating trade-offs and impacts across teams and timelines. Align on OKRs: Develop a culture of using OKRs to ensure team members align on the purpose of the work and cascade feedback related to risk and dependencies. 4. Innovation in Execution Leverage AI Tools: Utilize cutting-edge AI tools to accelerate requirements analysis, improve the quality of user story documentation, and enhance feature file generation. Mitigate Risk Proactively: Identify and flag potential risks and dependencies that could impact schedule or quality, and work with leadership to drive mitigation strategies. Domain Expertise: Proven background in Risk and Controls, Operational Risk, or Regulatory functions. Agile Product Expertise: Deep, hands-on expertise in managing a product backlog, writing high-quality user stories, story maps, and leading agile ceremonies (knowledge of SAFe Agile is preferred). Technical Fluency: A strong ability to understand technical concepts and engage in detailed discussions with engineering teams on feasibility and solutioning. Stakeholder Management: Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with demonstrated end-to-end ownership of deliverables. Education: Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Finance). A management degree such as an MBA is a plus. Preferred Skills & Certifications: Certifications: Industry-recognized certifications such as CSPO, A-CSPO, PSPO, SAFe POPM, or CBAP are highly desirable. Tooling: Expert-level proficiency with agile management software (e.g., Jira, Confluence ). AI in Practice: Hands-on experience using AI tools within a software development lifecycle is a significant advantage. Generative & Agentic AI Knowledge: Strong understanding of Generative AI and Agentic AI concepts and their applications in a product context. AI-Driven Capabilities: Experience contributing to initiatives involving AI-enabled or data-driven capabilities, such as intelligent monitoring, automation, or insights generation. Citi, the leading global financial services company, has some 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. Citi provides consumers, corporations, governments and institutions with a broad range of financial products and services, including consumer banking and credit, corporate and investment banking, securities brokerage, and wealth management. Citi Bank Retail Mortgage provides home lending services via our Citibank branches and centralized service centers. The Home Lending Officer role represents the Retail Mortgage business providing superior service to clients and referral partners and is responsible for originating high quality residential real estate loans for clients. This highly interactive role engages internally with retail branch partners, operations, community business development officers. This role drives mortgage sales and client relationships through engagement with clients, real estate agents, and other area referrers. Responsibilities: Consult with customers about their financial situation, financial and personal objectives and lending needs for the purpose of helping them achieve their home ownership goals. Collect and analyze information about the customer's financial situation, financial and personal goals, tolerance for risk and change, plans for the future, income, assets, debts, cash flow, and credit history. Analyze financial information for customers to make an initial assessment regarding whether the customer and the property may qualify for a particular lending solution. Make recommendations to customers about which lending solutions would best meet the customers' financial and personal objectives Advise customers about the consequences, risks, and benefits of alternative lending solutions. Promote Citi's brand, and promote Citi as the provider for lending and other financial solutions. This includes promoting Citi and its financial services to real estate agencies, builders, other referral sources, and customers. Visit customers outside of Citi's offices, with such visits to vary based on clientele, geography, market conditions, and other factors. Work as a team with all internal partners to support and grow our customers. Refer customers who seek financial services other than lending solutions to the appropriate Citi professionals. Partner with Operations teams to ensure the seamless transfer of the loan application in order to provide documents to the Processors and acquire any additional information needed by the Processors and/or Underwriters. Work with Processors/Closers and customers to ensure the timely closing of the customer's loan. Go outside to key referral relationships (Realtors, CPA's, Builders, etc). to drive mortgage business into the bank. The ability to communicate with customers about the proper documents and information needed to obtain a particular loan. Knowledge of the laws and regulations that govern consumer lending, including fair lending, privacy, and RESPA. Demonstrated customer service skills Strong relationship development and management skills Expertise of general lending products and overall mortgage industry.
